name: Folly-Fragment
geological_features: Irregular shape suggesting this body is a fragment of a larger planet
specific_features: Debris field of planetary fragments sharing the same orbit
description: Folly-Fragment is not truly a planet but the largest surviving piece of one, an irregular shard of rock and metal tumbling through space alongside a debris field of its former siblings. The shear faces where it separated from its parent body expose internal strata and crystalline core material that would normally be inaccessible without drilling to extraordinary depths.

Without atmosphere or meaningful gravity, the fragment exists in stark clarity, every surface feature sharp-edged and unweathered. The exposed core material catches starlight in prismatic flashes that make the fragment visible to the naked eye from neighboring worlds, a glittering reminder of catastrophic failure.

Geological analysis confirms the parent planet was destroyed approximately eight hundred years ago by an internal detonation consistent with an experimental energy source of immense power. The cultural records of three nearby civilizations all reference the event, describing it variously as divine punishment, a weapon test, or the inevitable consequence of a technology deployed without understanding.

The exotic matter trapped in the core material is of extraordinary scientific value, and the platinum deposits alone justify the cost of extraction operations. Yet the fragment's orbit is unstable and its rotation unpredictable, making every mining expedition a calculated gamble against the same reckless ambition that destroyed the world it once belonged to.
